characters.name: Darrow
characters.description: A young Red miner living in Lykos who dreams of freedom and excellence. He is haunted by the death of his father, who was executed for participating in a failed rebellion, and currently harbors a deep resentment for his uncle Narol.
key_events: Wins the Laurel of productivity for his mining clan
Engages in a physical fight with his uncle Narol
Expects to be awarded the Laurel by the Mine Magistrate
Experiences humiliation when Gamma is awarded the Laurel instead

characters.name: Eo
characters.description: Darrow's wife who is observant, beautiful, and deeply skeptical of the Society's control over their people. She possesses a keen intuition and often expresses concern regarding the harsh reality of their lives under the Tinpots.
key_events: Receives bread from Varlo the baker
Attempts to soothe Darrow's excitement regarding the Laurel
Displays apprehensive behavior during the Laureltide feast

characters.name: Uncle Narol
characters.description: Darrow's uncle and a former Helldiver who is bitter about his life and the futility of his brother's (Darrow's father) rebellion. He taught Darrow how to dance and move, but their relationship has devolved into resentment and alcohol-fueled conflict.
key_events: Plays the zither at the Laureltide dance

characters.name: Timony cu Podginus
characters.description: A small, copper-haired bureaucrat who manages the mining quotas and oversees the distribution of resources in the colony. He is condescending, detached, and displays a cruel indifference toward the suffering of the Red mining clans.
key_events: Mocks the Red clans for their simplicity
Awards the Laurel to Gamma instead of Darrow's clan

relationships.description: They are a devoted married couple with a deep emotional bond, though Darrow is currently frustrated by her lack of excitement regarding his achievements.
moments: Eo touches Darrow's hand and expresses suspicious concern about his pride

relationships.description: A strained relationship characterized by mutual disdain and old grudges. Darrow views his uncle as a weak coward, while Narol harbors bitterness over Darrow's rising status.
moments: The two engage in a physical fight during the Laureltide celebration

world_facts.name: Sons of Ares
world_facts.description: A terrorist organization blamed by the Society for bombings and acts of violence against mining crews, fighting against the established hierarchy.

world_facts.name: Laureltide
world_facts.description: A celebratory festival involving dancing, drinking, and the awarding of a Laurel branch to the most productive mining clan.

world_facts.name: Helldiver Status
world_facts.description: The elite miners responsible for extracting helium-3 from the Martian crust; their status is a point of pride and competition within the Red townships.

world_facts.name: The Society Colors
world_facts.description: A rigid, color-coded caste system where different colors hold specific roles, ranging from the Gold rulers to the Copper managers and Red laborers.

summary: In the township of Lykos, Darrow and his clan participate in the Laureltide dance, a rare celebration amidst their grueling life as Red miners. Darrow feels immense pride because he believes his clan has earned the Laurel for their outstanding mining productivity. As the community gathers in the Common, the atmosphere is a mix of merriment, drinking, and underlying tension, heightened by the constant presence of the Society's control through the holoCan (HC) broadcasts and the patrolling 'Tinpots' (Low-ranking guards). Darrow reflects on his complicated past, including his father's execution for leading a failed rebellion and his fraught relationship with his bitter uncle, Narol. The chapter establishes the disparity between the Reds and their rulers, the Coppers and Golds, as the local population waits for the arrival of the Mine Magistrate. When the Copper Magistrate, Timony cu Podginus, finally descends to the Common, he treats the mining community with detached condescension, mocking their simple lives while announcing which clans met their quotas. Despite the general expectation and Darrow's own confidence, the Magistrate awards the Laurel to the Gamma clan instead of Darrow's, leaving Darrow humiliated and his community slighted. The ending highlights the cruel indifference of the governing class and leaves the reader with a sense of Darrow's growing disillusionment and inner turmoil as he realizes the system is stacked against him and his people, despite his individual efforts.
